acceptance.renderer_crash_after_durable_write: PASS - connected Chromium's renderer was crashed with the CDP Page.crash command after the application-stage update committed and while its HTTP response was intentionally held.
acceptance.resumed_application_state: PASS - a fresh page recovered the manual application stage and append-only history from the same durable store; API readback before and after resume matched.
acceptance.truthful_application_state: PASS - the user-reported stage did not create an employer confirmation or change the application submission state.
acceptance.external_activity: PASS - browser requests were restricted to the isolated local API; no employer traffic or submission occurred.
acceptance.full_requirement: PARTIAL - product-worker process crash and browser-renderer crash are evidenced; physical host restart and whole-browser-process crash remain NOT_RUN.

validation.red_reproduction: NOT_APPLICABLE - existing durable tracking behavior was expected to satisfy the newly unverified crash scenario; this slice closes an acceptance-evidence gap rather than changing product code.
validation.initial_harness_attempt: FAIL - the first test run used Playwright's synchronous expect helper with an asynchronous locator. Corrected the harness to use async_expect; this did not indicate a product failure.
validation.browser_recovery_result: PASS - 1 connected Chromium renderer-crash recovery test.
validation.frontend_dependency_result: PASS - lockfile dependencies installed; zero vulnerabilities. Vitest warned that Node 25.9.0 is outside its declared engine range.
validation.full_python_suite: NOT_RUN - acceptance-only browser/test change; affected browser and integration suites were run.

environment.database: Temporary synthetic SQLite database; API remained running while Chromium's renderer was crashed and relaunched.
environment.docker_postgresql: NOT_RUN - no database code or migration changed.

limitations: Page.crash terminates the Chromium renderer target; it does not terminate the whole Chromium browser process or simulate a host restart.
No production source code changed because the observed durable application tracking path already recovered correctly in the connected crash scenario.
Issue #9 / MJ-REQ-008 remains OPEN/PARTIAL; full host restart, browser-process crash, live PostgreSQL and hosted verification remain unevidenced.
